knowledge.title: Propositional Logic Connectives
knowledge.content: Basic connectives: AND (∧), OR (∨), NOT (¬), IMPLIES (→), IFF (↔). Truth tables: p∧q is true iff both p and q are true. p∨q is true iff at least one is true. ¬p is the negation. p→q is false only when p is true and q is false. p↔q is true when p and q have the same truth value.

knowledge.title: Normal Forms: CNF and DNF
knowledge.content: Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF): conjunction of disjunctions (AND of ORs). Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF): disjunction of conjunctions (OR of ANDs). Every propositional formula can be converted to CNF or DNF. CNF is used in SAT solvers. Conversion uses De Morgan's laws and distributivity.

knowledge.title: Predicate Logic Quantifiers
knowledge.content: Universal quantifier (∀): 'for all x, P(x)' means P holds for every x. Existential quantifier (∃): 'there exists x such that P(x)' means P holds for at least one x. Negation rules: ¬∀x.P(x) ≡ ∃x.¬P(x) and ¬∃x.P(x) ≡ ∀x.¬P(x).

knowledge.title: Rules of Inference
knowledge.content: Modus Ponens: from p and p→q, infer q. Modus Tollens: from ¬q and p→q, infer ¬p. Hypothetical Syllogism: from p→q and q→r, infer p→r. Disjunctive Syllogism: from p∨q and ¬p, infer q. Resolution: from p∨q and ¬p∨r, infer q∨r. These are sound inference rules preserving truth.

knowledge.title: Temporal Logic Operators
knowledge.content: Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) operators: □ (always/G): P holds in all future states. ◇ (eventually/F): P holds in some future state. ○ (next/X): P holds in the next state. U (until): P U Q means P holds until Q becomes true. Used in model checking for verifying reactive systems.

knowledge.title: Fuzzy Logic and Membership Functions
knowledge.content: Fuzzy logic allows partial truth values in [0,1] instead of just {0,1}. Membership functions map inputs to degrees of membership. Common functions: triangular, trapezoidal, Gaussian. Fuzzy operators: AND = min(a,b), OR = max(a,b), NOT = 1-a. Used in control systems and approximate reasoning.
